audit.whatIsWrong: Two real defects: (1) both layers claim her W is a 'self-knockback' / 'her only mobility' — current Seismic Shove throws ENEMIES in a chosen direction, not herself; (2) the decisive interaction was never stated: Unraveled Earth mines STUN dashing enemies, so Vex's R recast through the minefield is a self-stun. Also zero sequencing cues (packet defect) and no digits in cooldowns.
audit.why: Riot text: W 'throws enemies within it in a direction of her choosing'; E 'if enemies dash through it or are knocked through it, the mines explode and stun them'. Vex R recast is a dash. W 14/12.5/11/9.5/8, E 14s, R 180/150/120. Note: kit flags mark Q/W as 'grounding' — Riot's descriptions say nothing about grounding (Worked Ground is her own resource); treated as a flag misfire and not asserted.
audit.corrected: Self-knockback claims removed from spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[3], early, whys[1]; the R-through-mines stun now anchors tradeBad, loading, cooldowns, donts and phases[4].why; real cooldowns added.

edits.before: An even poke war where his mobility advantage doesn't exist — trade marked rotations and let Gloom math grind the margins.
edits.after: An even poke war against a wall-surfer with no dash in lane — dodge the Threaded Volley lines and never dash across her mines.

edits.before: Win the marked-rotation war and convert R range into skirmish kills he can't match. Shorthand: Seismic Shove down, wave right, go.
edits.after: Win the poke war off her worked ground and never R through Unraveled Earth. Shorthand: Seismic Shove down (14s), wave right, go.

edits.before: Taliyah wins by landing Seismic Shove, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Taliyah wins by shoving you through her mines — Seismic Shove into Unraveled Earth is a stun you must never stand near.

edits.before: E-mark the contact, Q through the marked line for the fear, auto, walk — every trade he answers with a dash just schedules the next fear.
edits.after: Q her while she stands on worked ground — her Q there is one boulder, not a volley; step aside, answer with your 1200-range bolt, walk away.

edits.before: Spending the W pulse on poke spacing and then eating the real engage unfeared — the pulse is the matchup against everything that moves fast.
edits.after: R-dashing across Unraveled Earth — the mines detonate on dashes and stun you mid-execute, turning your kill window into her W-Q combo.

edits.before: Ahead, gloom harder: zone Taliyah with marked-rotation threat, R every skirmish his team starts, and reset through the kills — fed Vex makes mobility a typo.
edits.after: Ahead, gloom harder: zone Taliyah off the wave with Q threat, R every skirmish her team starts, and reset through the kills — she can't wall off a fed Vex forever.

edits.before: - Vex vs Taliyah - Track: Taliyah Seismic Shove. - Mark before you trade — unmarked rotations are half rotations. - No commits into Seismic Shove. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn’t open them.
edits.after: - Vex vs Taliyah - Track: Taliyah Seismic Shove. - Never R-dash through Unraveled Earth — the mines stun dashes. - No commits into Seismic Shove. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn't open them.

edits.before: Mark and bolt — your trades are honest and your passive makes his mobility dishonest. Bank Gloom procs like currency.
edits.after: Her Q costs mana and shoves — stand off the volley line, W-shield the chip, and trade back while she's stuck pushing.

edits.before: Luden's onward, hunt the skirmishes: R into river fights, fear the convergence, and reset off whatever dies. Your range is wherever the missile reaches.
edits.after: Luden's onward, match her Weaver's Wall roams — it's 180s at rank 1 against your 140s R. When her W is spent (14s early), step up: she has no peel left.

edits.before: - Taliyah Seismic Shove: matchup-defining — The shove into Unraveled Earth is her whole setup — sidestep it and the burst whiffs. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Personal Space has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Seismic Shove is 14s at rank 1 — the shove into Unraveled Earth is her whole setup; sidestep it and the burst whiffs. - Her E also runs 14s: while its mines litter the lane, hold your R recast — dashes through them are stunned. - Weaver's Wall is 180s; her roam threat sleeps without it.

edits.before: Taliyah's poke is her Q (Threaded Volley) spam, but each cast pushes the wave and burns mana, and her only escape is a self-knockback W off worked ground. Stand off her Q line, W-shield the chip, and answer with your own Q when she's shoving. Her W knock-up telegraphs hard; sidestep it and she has nothing to peel you with.
edits.after: Taliyah's poke is her Q (Threaded Volley) spam, but each cast pushes the wave and burns mana, and her W now throws YOU, not her — the danger is being shoved into Unraveled Earth for the mine stun. Stand off her Q line, W-shield the chip, and answer when she's shoving. Sidestep the telegraphed Seismic Shove and she has nothing to peel with.

edits.before: Her R is a roam and disengage wall, not a lane-kill tool, so at 6 your all-in threat outweighs hers. If she uses W to reposition, punish the moment she's out of dashes with an R-in, W, E-fear. Match her roams — your Shadow Surge crosses the map for a pick as well as her ult moves her.
edits.after: Her R is a roam and disengage wall, not a lane-kill tool, so at 6 your all-in threat outweighs hers. Punish whenever her W is spent with an R-in, W, E-fear — but recast around her mines, never through them. Match her roams — your Shadow Surge crosses the map for a pick as well as her ult moves her.

edits.before: Taliyah is a control mage who wants to poke and disengage; in a committed fight her mobility is limited to one W. Save your fear and R for when she W's, and burst her before her Q line can zone. Track her roams and R-follow to contest her map plays.
edits.after: Taliyah is a control mage who wants to poke and disengage; in a committed fight her peel is one Seismic Shove plus her minefield. Save your fear and R for after she shoves, and burst her before her Q line zones. Track her roams and R-follow to contest her plays.

edits.before: You're favoured if you respect her Q. Taliyah wants to chip you with Threaded Volley and shove, but every cast costs mana and pushes the wave toward you. Position off her Q line, shield the poke with W, and trade back when she's committed to shoving. Her W self-knockback is her only mobility and it's telegraphed, so there's little she can do when you step up.
edits.after: You're favoured if you respect her Q. Taliyah wants to chip you with Threaded Volley and shove, but every cast costs mana and pushes the wave toward you. Position off her Q line, shield the poke with W, and trade back when she's committed to shoving. Her Seismic Shove is telegraphed and it's her only peel, so there is little she can do when you sidestep and step up.

notes: Two real mechanical defects fixed: (1) both layers described Seismic Shove as a self-knockback / her only mobility — current W throws enemies, per Riot's text; (2) the decisive interaction — Unraveled Earth stuns dashing enemies, so Vex's R recast through the minefield is a self-stun — was absent everywhere and now anchors tradeBad, loading, cooldowns, donts and phases[4]. Full chart moved from all-Skill to all-Vex to agree with content win[] and packet at 53.46% WR; win[] untouched (already Vex). Kit flags mark her Q/W as 'grounding' but Riot's descriptions say nothing of the sort (Worked Ground is her own resource) — treated as a parser misfire, not asserted. Report edits beyond two are all lint-mandated pronoun/consistency fixes; report[3] is the only substantive rewrite. Content 'mid' still says 'when her W is spent she's immobile' — mild overstatement (she keeps P wall-speed) but directionally fine; left alone.
